audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers gave Kennen Level 1 and Levels 4-5, but whys[0] says level 1 is 'even-to-weak for you' and whys[3] says a pre-6 Kennen 'has to chip and respect rather than all-in'. The packet chart agrees: Skill at level 1, Nasus at 4-5.
audit.why: At level 1 Kennen has one Q point, no stun and a squishier body than Nasus; at 4-5 Nasus's HP and early stacks outgrow Kennen's pre-ult damage while Wither is already online.
audit.corrected: L1 Skill, L2 Kennen, L3 Kennen, Levels 4-5 Nasus, L6 Kennen, first item Nasus, 2+ items Nasus. Both layers proposed as a matched pair.

audit.why: Mirror finding reused: Slicing Maelstrom is a flat 120s at every rank, Fury of the Sands is 120/100/80, so Nasus out-cycles Kennen's ult from rank 2 onward. That is why level 6 is Kennen's single owned stage and first item is not.
audit.corrected: Spike order kept: Kennen at 2-3 and at 6, Nasus at first item and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive interactions were never stated: the range gap (Thundering Shuriken 950 vs Wither 700) and that Siphoning Strike is an auto-attack reset, so the wind-up — not the cast — is the cue to step out.
audit.why: Kennen kit Q range 950; Nasus W Wither 700 range, 15/14/13/12/11s. Nasus Q carries the autoReset flag, confirmed by the missingInteractions rule autoreset-burst-tell.
audit.corrected: Poke from outside 700 so Wither cannot answer, and read the Q wind-up as the reset tell.

audit.whatIsWrong: The late-game advice implies stacking resistances helps; missingInteractions flags resistances-invalidated on Fury of the Sands.
audit.why: Nasus's R carries the percentHealth flag — the storm's damage scales off health, so raw MR is not the answer to his ult window.
audit.corrected: wants.foe[2] now names Fury of the Sands and that its burn ignores stacked MR.

audit.why: packet flagged 'E-in Slicing Maelstrom' in wants.you[1] as a probable wrong name. Slicing Maelstrom is the correct Riot name for Kennen's R; the edit distance is only the attached prefix. False positive, matching the mirror's finding.

edits.before: Q-poke from range wins every melee matchup early. Identify how Nasus contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: No stun yet and his body is sturdier than yours — poke once at 950 and farm. Neither of you can commit anything at level 1.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Wither's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: His stacks and HP outgrow your pre-6 damage — chip, deny last-hits, and hold the all-in for level 6 instead of forcing it now.

edits.before: Wither answers your first-item burst directly: it slows your move and attack speed mid-R, so his Q lands while your kite dies.
edits.after: Wither (700 range, 15s at rank 1) answers your first item: it slows move and attack speed mid-R, so his Q lands while your kite dies.

edits.before: Wither is the problem item-for-item: once he hits 6 his W cripples your move and attack speed mid-R, blunting the burst you rely on.
edits.after: Wither is the problem item-for-item: 15s at rank 1, it cripples your move and attack speed mid-R and blunts the burst you rely on.

edits.before: Land Q poke from max range and chain a third Mark of the Storm stun before he can W-wither you
edits.after: Poke at 950, outside Wither's 700, and step back on his Q wind-up — Siphoning Strike is an auto reset

edits.before: Free-farm to a stacked Q and R lifesteal so his late-game drain eats your squishy body
edits.after: Free-farm to a stacked Q and Fury of the Sands, whose damage ignores the MR you stacked
